1.explanation:
• architecture.md: Gives the high-level project layout so you can locate the HTML report renderer and trace-gathering orchestration.
• error-reporting.md: Describes how runtime errors in gatherers and audits are caught and surfaced in the UI with the red exclamation icons and “Error” labels.
• understanding-results.md: Explains the structure of the Performance section, metrics, opportunities, and diagnostics rendering logic so you can see where the error placeholders are inserted.
• user-flows.md: Details the UI state transitions (e.g. selecting the Performance tab) and where error states are applied in the report flow.
• configuration.md: Shows how Lighthouse is configured (settings that enable/disable trace gatherers); misconfiguration here can reproduce the “did not run” condition.
• emulation.md: Documents device emulation prerequisites for traces (e.g. CPU/throttling settings). Omitting or mis‐setting these can cause the trace gatherer to fail, reproducing the runtime error.
1.bug_scenario: When running Lighthouse against https://www.cnn.com/, the Performance section immediately fails to render any metric values. Instead of numeric scores the UI shows a large red “!” icon and every metric (First Contentful Paint, Speed Index, Time to Interactive, etc.) is labeled “Error” with the message “Required traces gatherer did not run.” Scrolling down, the Opportunities and Diagnostics lists are similarly filled with error rows. Key UI elements involved are the report header icons, the Performance tab icon, the red error symbol and text for each metric row, and the collapsed “Opportunities”/“Diagnostics” list entries all showing an error state.
